decisions.decision: BiometricHelper gates on canCheckBiometrics only, not isDeviceSupported()
decisions.rationale: isDeviceSupported() returns true on emulators even without enrolled credentials, causing authenticate() to throw PlatformException → caught → returns false → Step 3 silently aborts. canCheckBiometrics is the correct signal for enrolled biometric hardware.
Previously set after biometric resolved — allowed 7 concurrent RSA compute() calls on fast-returning emulator. Early guard prevents re-entry during the async gap.

decisions.decision: TransferLogService writes to top-level transfer_logs, not users/{uid}/transfer_logs subcollection
decisions.rationale: Security rules only cover top-level transfer_logs. Subcollection path had no matching rule — PERMISSION_DENIED silently swallowed every call since service was created.

decisions.decision: user_repository.dart connections subcollection renamed to friendships
decisions.rationale: App migrated from connections to friendships. The old name had no Firestore rule and pointed to empty data. Used by admin ConnectionNodeMap widget.

decisions.decision: friendships rule extended with || isAdmin() on read
decisions.rationale: Admin dashboard ConnectionNodeMap streams other users' friendships for node visualization — owner-only read rule blocked it.

context_notes: Three layered bugs blocked Step 3 'Encrypt Key' button this session. (1) _fileEncrypted=false due to receiverReady race — fixed earlier. (2) _encryptingKey guard fired after biometric so 7 concurrent RSA calls queued. (3) Root cause: BiometricHelper.authenticate() returned false on emulator because isDeviceSupported()=true even without enrolled credentials — this silently aborted every Step 3 attempt. All fixes are committed. The Firestore rule audit was a side investigation — no impact on Step 3 directly, but two genuine bugs fixed (TransferLogService path, connections subcollection). UAT of Step 3 end-to-end has NOT been done yet.
